lessons.title: Preparing to plant a trial
lessons.html:
Preparing to plant a trial

A seed trial compares cultivars or breeding lines under the same conditions. The planting stage decides whether the trial will be fair. If the wrong seed goes into a plot, or plots are planted at different depths or spacings, the trial results are unreliable and a season is wasted.

Understand the trial plan

  • Read the trial protocol: number of entries, replications, plot size (rows and length), row spacing, plant population and planting date.
  • Study the field map. It shows where every plot is, its plot number and which entry goes into it. Entries are randomised in each replication.
  • Check that seed packets are prepared and sorted in planting order, each labelled with the plot number.

Prepare the field

  • The land should be prepared evenly: ploughed or ripped, levelled and free of weeds, as the protocol says.
  • Fertiliser is applied evenly across the whole trial at the rate in the protocol.
  • Choose an even part of the field. Avoid old kraals, wet spots, field edges and areas near trees.

Mark out the trial

  1. Measure the trial area with a tape measure or GPS.
  2. Put corner pegs and block markers.
  3. Mark plot boundaries and alleys between ranges.
  4. Check measurements twice. A mistake in marking moves every plot.

Prepare the planter

A plot planter or hand planter must be clean and set correctly: row spacing, seed spacing and depth. Check it on a test strip before planting the trial. Clean it so no seed from another trial remains.

Safety

Treated seed must be handled with gloves. Do not eat, drink or smoke while planting. Only trained operators drive tractors. Keep hands away from moving planter parts.

lessons.title: Planting the plots
lessons.html:
Planting the plots

Planting steps

  1. Start at the first plot on the field map. Check the plot number on the packet against the map before opening it.
  2. Empty the seed packet into the planter, or plant by hand at the correct spacing and depth.
  3. Plant the full row length and number of rows in the protocol.
  4. Make sure the planter is empty before moving to the next plot. Leftover seed in the planter gets mixed into the next plot.
  5. Keep empty packets in order. They show which plots have been planted.
  6. Put a plot label or stake at the start of each plot, with the plot number.

Even planting

  • Plant all plots on the same day if possible.
  • Keep planting depth the same. Seed planted too deep may not come up; too shallow may dry out.
  • Keep the tractor speed steady with a plot planter.
  • Firm the soil over the seed for good contact with moisture.

Border rows

Many trials plant border rows around the trial, using a common cultivar. These protect the outside plots from edge effects, such as more light or animal damage.

Recording

RecordExample
Trial name and locationMaize hybrid trial, farm and field
Planting dateDate planted
Planter settingsRow spacing, seed spacing, depth
Soil moisture at plantingDry, moist, wet
ProblemsPlots replanted, packet spilt, planter blocked

If something goes wrong in a plot, record the plot number and what happened immediately.

Completing

Count the empty packets against the map, clean the planter, return unused seed to the store, and give the records to the trial manager.

Key points

  • Follow the protocol and field map exactly.
  • Check the plot number on each packet before planting.
  • Empty the planter fully between plots.
  • Plant at even depth and spacing, ideally on one day.
  • Label every plot and record problems immediately.
